description: Producer-derived slow acceptance followed by higher Prepare. Observe acknowledgment and report for the same (origin,instance,acceptor); compare only reported phase against ACCEPTED. Retain command/ordering attributes as diagnostics, not duplicate properties.

harness.description: TestAssuranceAcceptedHistory invokes unmodified handlers and codecs over per-directed-link byte streams. Emits admitted acknowledgment and actual serialized PrepareReply; no goroutines or resources needing asynchronous cleanup are started.
semantic_changes: Constructor-equivalent bounded in-memory replicas instead of New network startup; initialized fields follow S_init/S_base.
Actual SendMsg writes to bufio.Writer over bytes.Buffer rather than TCP. Decode uses registered message New/Unmarshal.
Handler calls use an explicit serial schedule; recovery trigger is injected for a known unresolved slot instead of waiting on the execution scanner timer.
No protocol field is patched after initialization; proposals and all later messages use implementation producers.

legality.derivation: The harness initializes five replicas with constructor-equivalent empty protocol arrays and fixed N=5,F=2,Thrifty=true,Dreply=true,Durable=false. Array/channel capacities are reduced to 16 with only two used slots; no target code is replaced. Actual handlePropose calls create a pending conflicting command on row 1 and target command on row 0. The coordinator receives two actual decoded PreAcceptReply messages with different attributes and emits Accept through unchanged SendMsg/Marshal. Replica 2 admits it, sends matching AcceptReply, and coordinator 0 consumes that reply. The older independent row-1 PreAccept on link 1->2 and its reply are delivered before Prepare, preserving that directed byte-stream order. Replica 1 already knows the target slot, with status below COMMITTED and crtInstance covering it, which is the execution scanner eligibility for eventual recovery. The harness directly schedules startRecoveryForInstance as the recovery event and does not claim a measured timer threshold. It delivers the emitted higher Prepare to replica 2 and decodes its actual response. No target-instance mutation occurs between admitted acceptance and Prepare, apart from Prepare raising its promise. Pending messages remain undelivered in a finite asynchronous prefix; this is not a claim of fair infinite execution. Every delivered protocol payload was serialized by the source implementation. No test expected status is written to protocol state.
legality.applicability: Single-owner deterministic handler schedule models one permitted finite dispatch ordering. Real socket startup, execution worker and wall-clock timer loops are omitted; local entry and known stalled-slot prerequisites are explicitly checked. No application execution or completion guarantee is assumed.
unresolved: No end-to-end TCP deployment or timed recovery loop is run.
Source execution goroutine races are outside this serial local handler property.
alternatives: Deferred messages may later repair global progress, but cannot retroactively change the completed PrepareReply.

grounding.derivation: This is a local phase-history interface obligation, derived from the actual consumer rather than from the EPaxos name. The coordinator counts a matching-ballot AcceptReply as acceptance support (S_accept_reply). PrepareReply exposes Status as the phase of the retained value (S_wire, S_prepare). Recovery explicitly gives ACCEPTED a preservation branch before preacceptance/restart (S_recover_select 1228-1235,1255-1312), and S_try 1357-1360 states accepted history must not regress to preaccepted. Therefore an admitted and acknowledged Accept must establish acceptance that a later Prepare can recognize, absent an intervening value-changing request or decision. bal/vbal alone cannot substitute for Status at this consumer because its branch tests Status. This requirement concerns one acceptor report, not whether a quorum eventually decides a different value.
grounding.applicability: Initialized fixed-membership EPaxos acceptor, non-durable operation, existing uncommitted command and admitted Accept with matching acknowledgment. No intervening request changes that same instance value/phase; next Prepare has a greater ballot. Independent instances may progress.
unresolved: No separate protocol specification is used; applicability rests on the internal acceptance and recovery interface semantics.
The local report discrepancy alone does not establish a global agreement violation.
alternatives: The original coordinator retains ACCEPTED status and other replicas could preserve the value during recovery.
Command and ordering fields may remain intact even if phase reporting fails.

observable_properties.description: For each acknowledged acceptance admitted by accepted_ack, its completed higher-Prepare report must retain ACCEPTED phase (constant 3 in S_wire). Identity is independent of the phase and changing ballot.

uncertainties: The checker does not compare command/attribute content; these are logged as counterevidence and diagnostics.
It does not observe the later recovery selection or full-cluster safety consequence.
PrepareReply codec value-ballot omission is a separate sourced lead, not checked here.
